headline: MP Gazi Nazrul placed on 4-day remand after second wife's death
summary: The Satkhira-4 MP and his first wife are accused of torturing Mariam Khatun, leading to her suicide. Her father has filed a case for abetment of suicide.
details: Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and his first wife, Maksuda Begum, have been placed on remand after the death of his second wife, Mariam Khatun.
Mariam's body was recovered from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka, and her father, SM Masum Billah, has filed a case against the MP, his first wife, and a maternal uncle, Obaidur Rahman.

caption:
An MP and his first wife are in custody after the second wife's death. Her father alleges torture and abetment of suicide.

Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and his first wife, Maksuda Begum, have been placed on remand after the death of his second wife, Mariam Khatun.

Mariam's body was recovered from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka, and her father, SM Masum Billah, has filed a case against the MP, his first wife, and a maternal uncle, Obaidur Rahman.

The case, filed at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station, charges the accused under Section 306 of the Penal Code for the abetment of suicide.

Mariam's father alleged that his daughter was rarely spoken to and suffered significantly after marrying the MP in June, following the instigation of her uncle.

He claimed his daughter had expressed trust in her uncle but later felt betrayed and suffered because of that trust.

A Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate today placed Gazi Nazrul on a four-day remand and Maksuda Begum on a one-day remand following a police prayer for a seven-day remand.

The father is now calling for a proper investigation and justice for his daughter's death.

headline_marked: Two arrested after [[crude bomb blasts at Kamalapur railway station]]
headline: Two arrested after crude bomb blasts at Kamalapur railway station
summary: Police detained a former Chhatra League leader and a Jubo League activist for detonating cocktails on platform 2 to create public panic.
details: Police have arrested two individuals, identified as Mohammad Sakhawat Hossain Raihan (32) and Mohammad Sanmun (23), following crude bomb blasts at Kamalapur railway station.
The incident occurred on September 19 around 10:37 PM, when two cocktails exploded sequentially between pillars 29 and 30 on platform 2.
Raihan is a former organizational secretary of the banned Chhatra League's Shahjahanpur unit and a railway electrician who had been absent from work for three months.
Sanmun is described as an active member of the Shahjahanpur unit of the Jubo League. Both suspects have reportedly confessed to their involvement during preliminary questioning.
According to Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Harun or Rashid, the sabotage was intended to create fear among the public and support a 'lockdown' call.
Police are now investigating whether the suspects were involved in other blasts across the capital and are working to identify the entire network of financiers and coordinators.
caption:
Two men arrested after crude bombs exploded at Kamalapur railway station to 'create public panic'.

Police have arrested two individuals, identified as Mohammad Sakhawat Hossain Raihan (32) and Mohammad Sanmun (23), following crude bomb blasts at Kamalapur railway station.

The incident occurred on September 19 around 10:37 PM, when two cocktails exploded sequentially between pillars 29 and 30 on platform 2.

Raihan is a former organizational secretary of the banned Chhatra League's Shahjahanpur unit and a railway electrician who had been absent from work for three months.

Sanmun is described as an active member of the Shahjahanpur unit of the Jubo League. Both suspects have reportedly confessed to their involvement during preliminary questioning.

According to Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Harun or Rashid, the sabotage was intended to create fear among the public and support a 'lockdown' call.

Police are now investigating whether the suspects were involved in other blasts across the capital and are working to identify the entire network of financiers and coordinators.
